scope: Capability groups, not individual property count or a promise of complete CSS/SVG conformance. Existing/partial status is based on source inspection. API and phase proposals remain provisional until usage examples and implementation verification.
api_constraint: Preserve direct typed data, caller-owned memory and control flow, independently callable passes and optional high-level conveniences. Caches, registries and interning are optional. Study Casey Muratori references and write usage code before public API changes.

baseline.integrated: The audited standard path already provides the named capability; backend and combination limits still apply.
baseline.low_level: A lower-level operation already exists, but broader front-end integration or convenience is needed.
baseline.partial: Substantial related support exists, but options, semantics, combinations or coverage need extending.
baseline.not_found: No general built-in implementation of this capability was identified in the inspected baseline; this is a scoped source-audit finding, not proof that custom host code cannot do it.
baseline.application_authored: Existing extension paths allow applications to construct this behavior, but no common built-in styling contract provides it.

action.retain: Preserve existing behavior and carry it through new paths.
action.integrate: Expose existing operations through supported caller paths.
action.extend: Broaden an existing implementation or its semantics.
action.optional: Keep as a separately selected extension or application layer.

phase.P0: Correctness, geometry, value identity, capacities and capability contracts
phase.P1: Expose existing capabilities; direct style composition, themes, states and parts
phase.P3: Advanced layout, responsiveness, vectors and motion
phase.P4: Optional layers, masks, compositing and filters
phase.P5: Specialist/platform/document extensions selected by actual demand

items.title: Typed property metadata and support contract
items.baseline_detail: Style/TextStyle, theme helpers and feature usage exist, but no unified property metadata and support contract spanning layout/text/paint/parts was found.
requirements: Compile-time property metadata without a mandatory runtime registry
items.recommendation: Define semantics before expanding property count; preserve a direct plain-data path with compile-time metadata and no required runtime registry.
items.acceptance: Every accepted property has a consumer, stated fallback or rejection; a paint-only token change does not trigger layout.

items.title: Caller-owned optional style storage
items.baseline_detail: Tree uses optional Extra rows and compact Look storage; DESIGN requires caller-owned memory and a dependency-free Tier 0.
items.recommendation: Preserve the compact ordinary widget path; do not place every option in every node.
items.acceptance: Exhausting a declared pool returns a deterministic failure without allocation, corruption or silently missing properties.

items.title: Explicit presence and inheritance
items.baseline_detail: theme.Inherited resolves caller-owned color/px columns but treats zero as inherit; explicit transparent and zero are ambiguous.
items.recommendation: Replace sentinel semantics with explicit presence while preserving existing callers through an adapter.
items.acceptance: A transparent literal stays transparent under a colored parent; inherit follows the parent; an explicit override stops propagation.

items.title: Role-preserving semantic color tokens
items.baseline_detail: Six color roles exist; recolor matches raw packed color values and requires distinct source colors.
items.recommendation: Extend existing roles and preserve identity through lowering rather than remapping equal raw colors.
items.acceptance: Two roles can share the same original RGBA value and diverge on theme change while an equal literal remains unchanged.

items.title: Spacing, typography and shape token scales
items.baseline_detail: Five-step spacing/radius/text-size scales and density exist; richer typography and component scales are not unified.
items.recommendation: Retain current scale APIs and add semantic aliases plus composite typography recipes.
items.acceptance: Changing density updates dependent spacing and hit targets without accidentally scaling physical strokes or fixed assets.

items.title: Scoped themes and deterministic precedence
items.baseline_detail: Runtime themes, per-widget overrides and compile-time folded themes exist; a general layered scoped resolver is absent.
items.recommendation: Document precedence and preserve component-local overrides during a global theme change.
items.acceptance: A nested theme changes its descendants only; the inspector can identify the winning source for conflicting values.

items.title: Reusable widget part styles
items.baseline_detail: Widgets author their own visuals and options; a consistent reusable part/variant/state contract was not found.
items.recommendation: Allow direct part parameters and optional shared recipes without requiring a full node allocation or global registry for each decorative mark.
items.acceptance: A shared thumb recipe styles slider and range handles without changing their value or input semantics.

items.title: Named variants and reusable component recipes
items.baseline_detail: Widget-specific variants and options exist, but naming and override composition are not unified.
requirements: Plain recipe values; optional references for reuse
items.recommendation: Allow direct plain-data recipe composition plus optional pre-resolved reuse; keep behavior separate and avoid mandatory registry setup.
items.acceptance: Combining a small destructive button variant with a local text-color override preserves the remaining recipe values.

items.title: Combinable state-dependent styling
items.baseline_detail: theme.States contains eight hover/held/focused combinations; widgets have local states and a11y exposes additional semantic states.
requirements: Direct ordered state-rule evaluation; optional caller-owned cache of reached combinations
items.recommendation: Resolve ordered overrides without allocating a table for every theoretical state combination.
items.acceptance: Selected plus hovered plus keyboard-focused retains selection and visible focus; disabled behavior cannot be enabled by a paint override.

items.title: Shared style handles and targeted invalidation
items.baseline_detail: Theme/build helpers and incremental layout exist; no unified style dependency resolver was found.
items.recommendation: Offer caller-owned caching as an optional acceleration of the direct plain-data path; do not require a global style registry or theme manager.
items.acceptance: Hovering one control in a large list recomputes its affected style values without re-resolving unrelated rows.

items.title: Unified runtime and compile-time authoring
items.baseline_detail: Typed styles and both runtime/comptime front ends exist; advanced side tables require manual finishing sequences.
items.recommendation: Preserve fine-grained passes and add useful diagonal conveniences; advanced use must not require a manager, object graph or mandatory caching.
items.acceptance: One styled control produces equivalent supported draw output in runtime and compile-time paths with explicit unsupported diagnostics.

items.title: Optional design-token interchange
items.baseline_detail: No built-in DTCG import or external typed token compiler was identified in the audited source.
items.recommendation: Keep interchange outside Tier 0 and generate constants or bounded data; DTCG is a Community Group specification.
items.acceptance: Alias cycles and type mismatches fail during import; generated tokens preserve role identity and deterministic output.

items.title: Optional CSS-like authoring compiler
items.baseline_detail: Core is typed Zig; markup/parser documents describe future authoring work rather than a complete stylesheet system.
items.recommendation: Add only with a concrete consumer; CSS syntax must lower to the same typed IR instead of adding per-frame parsing.
items.acceptance: Unsupported syntax is diagnosed; accepted rules compile deterministically and never scan source strings during rendering.

items.title: Computed-style and dependency inspector
items.baseline_detail: Source has devtools-related facilities and checks, but no unified computed-style provenance contract was identified.
items.recommendation: Compile provenance out of release profiles; emit bounded diagnostic records rather than runtime callbacks.
items.acceptance: A conflicting state/variant override can be explained to the exact source and invalidation reason without changing program behavior.

items.title: Preferred, minimum and maximum dimensions
items.baseline_detail: Core Style supports fit/px/grow/pct and min/max; aspect ratio is in the flex side table.
items.recommendation: Retain existing dimensions and expose aspect ratio while specifying over-constrained outcomes.
items.acceptance: Conflicting min/max and aspect ratio produce documented deterministic sizes; percentage values are not incorrectly advertised as new.

items.title: Intrinsic content measurement semantics
items.baseline_detail: Fit sizing and text/image measurement exist; complete CSS intrinsic-size keywords and semantics are not exposed.
items.recommendation: Provide a native intrinsic-sizing contract before considering exact CSS compatibility.
items.acceptance: A wrapped label and unwrapped label report different meaningful minima, and measured sizes agree with final line layout.

items.title: Relative length units and bounded expressions
items.baseline_detail: Core supports pixel and percentage sizes; broader relative units and expression evaluation are not unified.
items.recommendation: Use validated bounded expressions, not an unbounded interpreter in hot layout loops.
items.acceptance: Changing text scale affects font-relative spacing while device-pixel strokes stay fixed; indefinite percentage bases follow documented behavior.

items.title: Per-edge padding and margins
items.baseline_detail: Core has four-side padding; flex side tables contain non-collapsing margins.
items.recommendation: Expose existing margins and document non-collapsing native semantics; choose explicit policy for negative values.
items.acceptance: Margins influence placement without changing paint content bounds; nested margins never collapse implicitly.

items.title: Independent gaps and line spacing
items.baseline_detail: Core has one gap; grid has row/column gaps and flex has wrapping-related spacing.
items.recommendation: Allow separate axes while preserving the current single-gap shorthand.
items.acceptance: A wrapping panel can have different item and line spacing, and orientation changes map each gap predictably.

items.title: Direction-aware logical edges and dimensions
items.baseline_detail: Rtl supports inherited LTR/RTL, logical inline padding and mirroring; other logical properties are not generalized.
items.recommendation: Broaden the existing RTL helper rather than adding a second direction model.
items.acceptance: Switching LTR to RTL mirrors logical margins and anchors while explicitly physical left/right values obey documented precedence.

items.title: Flex basis, growth and shrink semantics
items.baseline_detail: Core grow/shrink and flex weighted shrink/bounded two-pass regrow exist; no named basis and no full CSS freeze algorithm.
items.recommendation: Keep the bounded native profile and add richer behavior only behind an explicit algorithm choice.
items.acceptance: Unequal shrink weights respect minimum sizes; native bounded results and any CSS-compatible results are separately documented and tested.

items.title: Wrapping, line layout and baseline alignment
items.baseline_detail: Flex supports row wrapping, self cross alignment and baseline on non-wrapping rows; limitations are real.
items.recommendation: Expose present wrapping first and extend column/multiline baseline behavior with explicit semantics.
items.acceptance: Wrapped rows of mixed font sizes align by the selected baseline without clipping; unsupported profile combinations reject explicitly.

items.title: Container and item alignment distribution
items.baseline_detail: Core main/cross alignment covers start/center/end; flex/grid add limited self/stretch/line behavior.
items.recommendation: Distinguish content distribution from individual item alignment.
items.acceptance: Space-evenly includes both outer gaps; safe alignment keeps overflowing content reachable instead of centering it offscreen.

items.title: Public integration of bounded grid
items.baseline_detail: Grid exports px/fit/fr tracks, spans and sparse row-order placement with one sizing round and no implicit growth.
items.recommendation: Expose existing grid honestly as a bounded native layout rather than CSS Grid conformance.
items.acceptance: A normal frontend can build a spanned grid; out-of-capacity placement preserves the documented overflow flag and never writes outside buffers.

items.title: Richer grid tracks and placement
items.baseline_detail: The audited grid intentionally lacks these richer track and placement features.
items.recommendation: Implement as a richer selectable profile after basic grid integration.
items.acceptance: Automatic track creation respects capacity, named areas resolve deterministically and dense placement never changes semantic focus order implicitly.

items.title: Subgrid alignment across nested components
items.baseline_detail: No subgrid contract was found in the bounded grid implementation.
items.recommendation: Make subgrid optional and dependency-driven; a simple shared-column helper may satisfy early use cases.
items.acceptance: Nested form rows align to parent tracks and update after a parent resize without indefinite layout retries.

items.title: Out-of-flow placement and containing blocks
items.baseline_detail: Style.float and offset exist; float places outside flow at the parent content origin, not a complete positioning model.
items.recommendation: Preserve float semantics and add explicit position modes instead of overloading one boolean.
items.acceptance: An absolutely positioned badge is excluded from sibling layout and resolves percentage insets against the documented containing box.

items.title: Menus and popovers anchored to geometry
items.baseline_detail: overlay exports anchors/pivots, offsets, viewport flipping and zstack facilities.
items.recommendation: Integrate existing anchors into consistent popover/menu recipes; extend fallback policies without callback allocation.
items.acceptance: A tooltip near each viewport edge chooses a visible fallback and remains anchored after its target moves.

items.title: Fixed and sticky positioning
items.baseline_detail: The float flag and overlay helpers do not establish a general fixed/sticky style contract.
items.recommendation: Define which coordinate spaces and scroll ancestors govern these modes.
items.acceptance: A sticky table header remains within its scroll container and stops at its end; nested clipping and input coordinates remain correct.

items.title: Consistent paint and hit layer order
items.baseline_detail: Layers uses 256 global levels inheriting the parent maximum; layered paint and hit helpers exist but are separate paths.
requirements: Explicit global versus local context semantics
items.recommendation: Connect existing layered paint and hit paths before adding richer stacking-context semantics.
items.acceptance: The visually topmost overlapping eligible widget receives input; global level behavior is not mislabeled nested CSS isolation.

items.title: Visibility, layout and input participation
items.baseline_detail: Clipping/visibility flags and opacity exist, but a unified author-facing contract separating participation modes was not found.
items.recommendation: Define independent meanings instead of using zero opacity as a universal hiding mechanism.
items.acceptance: Hidden-reserved content keeps space; excluded content does not; transparent interactive content follows its explicit hit policy.

items.title: Overflow and scrolling semantics
items.baseline_detail: Core scroll/clip fields and scroll helpers exist; rounded/nested clips have separate rendering limits.
items.recommendation: Unify existing scroll and clip flags without claiming clip geometry fixes that belong to the renderer.
items.acceptance: A clip-only container cannot scroll programmatically by accident; automatic bars use the same content extents as input scrolling.

items.title: Containment and virtualized measurement boundaries
items.baseline_detail: Incremental layout and virtual-list widgets exist; general containment/responsive dependency semantics are not exposed.
items.recommendation: Reuse virtualized paths while defining which ancestor measurements are independent of descendants.
items.acceptance: Offscreen row styling does not force realization of every row; changing a size-affecting token updates total scroll extent correctly.

items.title: Custom layout through explicit passes
items.baseline_detail: Frame.finish permits caller-performed layout and core design requires data-oriented caller-owned passes.
items.recommendation: Standardize data exchange and compile-time specialization; do not inject hidden allocation or callback dispatch into Tier 0.
items.acceptance: A custom radial layout can use supplied rows and finish through normal paint/input processing with no runtime per-widget callback or hidden allocation.

items.title: Logical geometry and pixel rounding policy
items.baseline_detail: Layout finalization snaps rectangles; transformations and text paths introduce additional geometry considerations.
items.recommendation: Keep fractional geometry until the chosen raster stage and define rounding consistently across sibling distribution.
items.acceptance: Fractional scaling does not accumulate gaps across a long row, and caret geometry agrees with painted glyph metrics.

items.title: Viewport and container style conditions
items.baseline_detail: Applications can inspect viewport/platform and choose typed styles; no shared declarative condition resolver was found.
items.recommendation: Use typed predicates with explicit dependencies; dock panels should respond to their own size.
items.acceptance: Resizing one dock panel changes its compact variant without restyling unrelated panels or creating size-query oscillation.

items.title: Environment and input-capability conditions
items.baseline_detail: Platform dark/accent helpers, density and accessibility settings exist; a uniform condition interface does not.
items.recommendation: Integrate existing helpers and expose only host-observed capabilities without pretending all backends have every preference.
items.acceptance: Changing a hover capability updates affected recipes only; unknown is distinguishable from an explicit false preference.

items.title: Safe-area and viewport occlusion inputs
items.baseline_detail: Overlay placement uses viewport constraints; richer host occlusion/safe-area data was not identified as a style contract.
items.recommendation: Let the host provide geometry; keep OS discovery outside Tier 0.
items.acceptance: A focused input and its popup remain within the supplied usable rectangle when a keyboard occlusion region appears.

items.title: Specialized native and document layouts
items.baseline_detail: Core supplies row/column, bounded flex/grid and explicit pass escape hatches; these specialized models are not general built-ins.
items.recommendation: Build actual-use-case modules without burdening every node or claiming complete document layout.
items.acceptance: An enabled module publishes its supported semantics and capacity limits; disabled modules add no per-node storage requirement.

items.title: Advanced text in the normal frame path
items.baseline_detail: TextStyle exposes px/color/font/wrap; normal Frame.end uses Mono while advanced layout requires manual stage/finish.
items.recommendation: Expose existing text algorithms before implementing replacements.
items.acceptance: An ordinary frame can render and measure a centered wrapped proportional-font label with the same metrics used by hit queries.

items.title: Family, resource and style matching
items.baseline_detail: Font handles, OpenType loading, OS discovery and fallback chains exist; no high-level family/style matching contract is unified.
requirements: Caller-supplied face/family catalogs and matching metadata; optional registry adapter
items.recommendation: Keep explicit handles available and add deterministic resource matching above the existing loader.
items.acceptance: A missing requested family chooses the documented fallback; loading a new matching font invalidates dependent metrics without corrupting handles.

items.title: Font weight, width and slant selection
items.baseline_detail: opentype.Style selects bold/italic bits; named weights, stretch and synthesis policy are not exposed through TextStyle.
items.recommendation: Prefer actual font faces and make synthetic bold/oblique an explicit fallback policy.
items.acceptance: A requested weight selects the correct face when present and follows the stated synthesis fallback when absent.

items.title: Extended font formats and variable/color fonts
items.baseline_detail: Loader supports TrueType outlines and TTC face selection and explicitly rejects OTTO/CFF; general variable/color-font support is not established.
items.recommendation: Keep format support explicit and enable additional formats per profile rather than implying all OpenType is supported.
items.acceptance: Unsupported formats fail clearly; enabled variable axes alter geometry and metrics with distinct cache keys.

items.title: Shaping feature and run-property control
items.baseline_detail: Built-in Features exposes liga/kern/mark/mkmk; optional HarfBuzz guesses run properties and uses default features.
items.recommendation: Expose existing toggles and explicit run metadata while distinguishing the capabilities of each shaper.
items.acceptance: Toggling a supported ligature feature changes the intended run without changing unrelated text; unsupported features are reported by profile.

items.title: Bidi, script and language integration
items.baseline_detail: Unicode script/bidi modules and paragraph reorder exist; front-end itemization and shaper composition require explicit sequencing.
items.recommendation: Reuse existing Unicode machinery and make the advanced text profile sequencing explicit.
items.acceptance: Arabic mixed with Latin labels and numbers preserves correct visual order and stable logical selection indices.

items.title: Cluster-aware font fallback
items.baseline_detail: Fallback Chain/Runs exists but built-in fallback resolves per character, requiring care for joined/variation/complex sequences.
items.recommendation: Preserve shaping context across fallback and avoid splitting sequences that require a single font decision.
items.acceptance: A supported joined emoji or base-plus-mark sequence is not broken by per-code-point fallback when one font can render the sequence.

items.title: Grapheme-safe indexing and editing
items.baseline_detail: Standard text widgets already use edit.Editor, with grapheme-based movement/backspace/delete and optional bidi mapping; Unicode grapheme/word and cluster-aware wrapping modules also exist. Consistent mappings and conformance across all new styling/truncation paths still need verification.
items.recommendation: Preserve existing algorithms through all new styling paths rather than reimplementing byte-based shortcuts.
items.acceptance: Caret movement, backspace and ellipsis never split an extended grapheme cluster, including combined marks and supported emoji sequences.

items.title: Paragraph alignment and justification
items.baseline_detail: lines exposes alignment factor, justify and direction; Stack.layoutAt initializes start alignment.
items.recommendation: Expose existing alignment and justification through the normal API; add missing last-line semantics explicitly.
items.acceptance: Centered, end-aligned and justified paragraphs use the same measured line widths as painting, including RTL runs.

items.title: Whitespace, newlines and tabs
items.baseline_detail: No-wrap, mandatory newline breaks, a final empty line after a trailing newline and hanging trailing-space behavior already exist. Configurable collapse/preserve policy and tab sizing/stops remain extensions.
items.recommendation: Apply visual whitespace policy without rewriting the stored document.
items.acceptance: Preserved tabs align predictably and copying a visually collapsed label retains the documented original-text behavior.

items.title: Line-breaking policies and hyphenation
items.baseline_detail: Unicode line breaking and cluster-safe emergency wrapping exist; richer policies/hyphenation are not a unified public contract.
items.recommendation: Retain the existing fast breaker; make language dictionaries and balanced wrapping optional.
items.acceptance: Emergency wrapping preserves clusters; a discretionary hyphen appears only at a chosen break and layout remains bounded.

items.title: Truncation and maximum visible lines
items.baseline_detail: lines has maximum-line ellipsizing and metrics; TextStyle and normal Frame.end do not expose the complete capability.
items.recommendation: Integrate existing ellipsize/max-line support first; add start/middle modes with explicit logical-direction behavior.
items.acceptance: A middle-truncated path preserves its selected suffix, never splits a cluster and exposes its full value to copying/accessibility.

items.title: Line height, leading and baseline metrics
items.baseline_detail: Paragraph metrics and manual modification are available, but no unified style contract controls these metrics.
items.recommendation: Distinguish logical line boxes from ink bounds and expose metrics needed by component alignment.
items.acceptance: Mixed font sizes share the selected baseline; larger line spacing avoids glyph/caret clipping and produces matching measured height.

items.title: Letter and word spacing
items.baseline_detail: A unified TextStyle spacing contract was not identified; existing paragraph metrics can be manually altered.
items.recommendation: Adjust advances with script-aware rules and keep shaping and spacing responsibilities explicit.
items.acceptance: Spacing changes update measured width, hit positions and painting consistently without separating required joining behavior.

items.title: Rich text shaping runs versus paint spans
items.baseline_detail: Spans supports byte-range font/size/color changes but every span boundary interrupts shaping, including color-only boundaries.
items.recommendation: Do not reshape or break ligatures merely because a color/highlight boundary changes.
items.acceptance: Adding a color-only highlight preserves glyph selection, positions and paragraph width; paint segmentation alone changes.

items.title: Text decorations
items.baseline_detail: No unified decoration style contract was identified alongside existing rich spans and text primitives.
items.recommendation: Use shared decoration records and preserve shaping; keep less common emphasis marks optional.
items.acceptance: Underline offset and thickness follow resized text; decoration bounds participate in damage and do not alter glyph metrics.

items.title: Inline objects and baseline shifts
items.baseline_detail: Rich spans cover font/size/color; generic inline objects and styled baseline-shift records were not identified.
items.recommendation: Use caller-supplied measured rows for inline objects rather than runtime measurement callbacks.
items.acceptance: An inline icon and subscript affect line height correctly and remain selectable/navigable according to the documented index policy.

items.title: Foreground, background and highlight paint for text
items.baseline_detail: Rich spans support color; general text paint objects, backgrounds and complex paint propagation are not unified.
items.recommendation: Reuse the general paint system and avoid breaking shaping at paint-only boundaries.
items.acceptance: Changing a highlight background or foreground role repaints without changing shaped glyphs; unsupported text paint kinds fail explicitly.

items.title: Editable text visual parts
items.baseline_detail: Textfield/textarea include caret, selection and IME plumbing; a uniform part-style contract is absent.
items.recommendation: Keep text input semantics in the edit system and expose visuals through common part/state recipes.
items.acceptance: A theme swap updates caret/selection/composition appearance without losing composition text, selection endpoints or keyboard focus.

items.title: Locale-aware display text transformations
items.baseline_detail: No unified locale-aware transform style and mapping contract was identified.
items.recommendation: Treat transformation as a display layer with explicit locale and preserve original content.
items.acceptance: Locale-sensitive case conversion can change displayed length while selection/copy behavior remains defined against the original text.

items.title: OpenType typographic variants
items.baseline_detail: Built-in shaping supports a limited feature set; arbitrary advanced feature selection is not exposed in TextStyle.
items.recommendation: Offer useful numeric variants first for engineering tables while preserving a low-level feature list.
items.acceptance: Tabular digits align changing values without layout jitter when supported; unsupported variants are diagnosed rather than falsely advertised.

items.title: Text cache and invalidation contract
items.baseline_detail: Shaping/cache/layout modules exist; a comprehensive new styling dependency contract is needed across public paths.
items.recommendation: Reuse current caches and invalidate only stages dependent on changed properties, allowing boundary-sensitive reshaping where required.
items.acceptance: Color-only changes reuse shaped runs; font-feature/language changes invalidate them; width changes yield correct line breaks and caret positions.

items.title: Vertical writing and ruby annotations
items.baseline_detail: RTL helpers mirror the x-axis and Unicode bidi exists, but this is not a complete writing-mode/ruby layout system.
items.recommendation: Add a separate advanced text profile only when applications require it.
items.acceptance: Vertical text uses correct glyph orientation and logical edges; ruby contributes documented line extents without disrupting base-text indexing.

items.title: Specialist document typography
items.baseline_detail: No general document compositor or these specialized typography contracts were found in the audited UI text pipeline.
items.recommendation: Keep these outside the native control core and add modules for demonstrated consumers.
items.acceptance: An optional module declares a bounded supported subset and can be disabled without adding ordinary label storage or work.

items.title: Pointer cursor appearance
items.baseline_detail: Context.Cursor already defines arrow, pointer, text, grab and horizontal/vertical resize; Frame.setCursor emits host cursor intent with last-request-wins semantics, and text widgets use it. More cursor types, custom hotspots and style-driven eligibility/ordering remain extensions.
items.recommendation: Resolve cursor intent as data and let the platform host apply supported cursors.
items.acceptance: Overlapping widgets select the topmost eligible cursor; custom hotspots are scaled consistently and unsupported cursors use an explicit fallback.

items.title: Visual and hit-target geometry policy
items.baseline_detail: Hit testing includes near-target selection with topmost tie-breaking and configurable global touch slop (default eight logical pixels). Style.transform remains paint-only; per-node expansion, shape policies and transform-consistent input remain extensions.
items.recommendation: Separate usable hit geometry from decorative geometry and define overlap priority for enlarged targets.
items.acceptance: A visually transformed button receives clicks where it is painted; expanded neighboring targets resolve overlap deterministically.

items.title: Keyboard-visible focus styling policy
items.baseline_detail: Focus already tracks modality-sensitive visibility; key/pointer transitions update it, ring respects it, and runtime supports always_show_focus. Reuse this state for consistent parts/recipes; add focus-within and broader composed decoration/reveal behavior.
requirements: Reuse and propagate existing input-modality/focus state
items.recommendation: Preserve focus semantics and use dedicated outline decoration from the paint system.
items.acceptance: Keyboard navigation produces a visible focus indicator without changing layout; hover/selected states cannot erase it unintentionally.

items.title: Behavioral state and visual-state consistency
items.baseline_detail: Widgets and accessibility records expose several states, but styling state recipes are narrower and inconsistent.
items.recommendation: Have styles observe semantic state; do not treat disabled colors as the mechanism that disables input.
items.acceptance: A disabled control is non-activating regardless of its colors, and read-only text can preserve allowed selection/copy behavior.

items.title: High contrast and system color palettes
items.baseline_detail: High-contrast settings and contrast checks already exist; high-contrast light/system-color policies need broader integration.
items.recommendation: Extend existing accessibility palette handling while preserving intended state distinctions beyond hue.
items.acceptance: Switching high contrast preserves legible text and identifiable control boundaries in both light and dark profiles.

items.title: User text scale and spacing tolerance
items.baseline_detail: Settings already supplies text scale; richer spacing options and every component layout must participate consistently.
items.recommendation: Retain text-scale support and make all public text/control paths tolerant of user overrides.
items.acceptance: Large text and user spacing settings do not clip labels, hide values or make primary controls unreachable.

items.title: Reduced motion and transparency preferences
items.baseline_detail: Reduced motion already affects runtime animations; reduced-transparency and general effect fallback policies are not unified.
items.recommendation: Connect existing reduced-motion behavior to the resolver and add reduced-transparency policy without redesigning motion internals.
items.acceptance: Preference changes replace translucent surfaces with readable opaque equivalents and preserve already-supported reduced-motion behavior.

items.title: State indication beyond color
items.baseline_detail: Widgets provide marks and accessibility states; a consistent recipe contract enforcing multi-channel state indication is not established.
items.recommendation: Provide useful default recipes that remain understandable when colors are unavailable or overridden.
items.acceptance: Error, checked and selected states remain distinguishable in a grayscale/system-color rendering and agree with accessibility state.

items.title: Scrollbar part appearance
items.baseline_detail: Scroll widget has a vertical track/thumb and keyboard controls; bar_px is fixed at 8.
items.recommendation: Replace fixed paint constants with part recipes and keep thumb hit geometry usable.
items.acceptance: A themed scrollbar supports distinct hover/drag states and never paints a thumb below the configured minimum length.

items.title: Scrollbar axes, placement and gutters
items.baseline_detail: Current widget primarily exposes a vertical bar with fixed width; no complete placement/gutter contract is present.
items.recommendation: Keep reserved space independent from visibility and avoid oscillating layout when bars appear.
items.acceptance: Content near an overflow threshold settles without repeated bar show/hide cycles; RTL placement and two-axis corner geometry are correct.

items.title: Optional scroll behavior policies
items.baseline_detail: Lower-level scroll helpers and widget input exist; broad unified snap/overscroll/chain style policies were not established by the audit.
items.recommendation: Keep behavior adjacent to styling and preserve caller control over scrolling mechanics.
items.acceptance: Nested scroll containers follow an explicit chaining policy; snap targets remain reachable and reduced-motion preferences are respected.

items.title: Focused target reveal and scroll anchoring
items.baseline_detail: Focus, scroll and keyboard helpers exist; a unified cross-container reveal/anchoring contract was not identified.
items.recommendation: Use an explicit caller-sequenced reveal pass rather than hidden recursive callbacks.
items.acceptance: Tabbing to an offscreen input reveals it through nested scrollers without unexpectedly jumping unrelated containers.

items.title: Everyday control part recipes
items.baseline_detail: All these widgets largely exist with local paint/options, but no consistent shared part recipe surface spans them.
requirements: Shared part vocabulary and direct part recipes; optional lookup
items.recommendation: Standardize styling of existing controls while retaining widget-specific semantics.
items.acceptance: A shared theme can style all listed controls and their disabled/focused/selected states without copying widget implementations.

items.title: Navigation and overlay part recipes
items.baseline_detail: Menu, popover, tooltip, tabs, breadcrumb, toast and related widgets exist with individual options.
items.recommendation: Expose parts consistently and reuse anchor, typography and paint systems.
items.acceptance: A theme change updates every popup/navigation part while preserving accelerator alignment, overflow behavior and focus navigation.

items.title: List, tree and table visual parts
items.baseline_detail: List/tree/table/vlist widgets exist, but broad cross-widget part styling is not unified.
items.recommendation: Keep row/cell style metadata compact and independent from materialized visible widgets.
items.acceptance: Alternating and selected styles track logical rows after virtualization/reordering, while keyboard focus remains independently visible.

items.title: Extensible EDA and editor visual vocabulary
items.baseline_detail: Custom materials/draw commands and common widgets provide extension paths; a domain-specific EDA style catalog is not built in.
items.recommendation: Allow application-defined part/token values or IDs so domain recipes do not expand core Style for every object kind; registration and shared lookup remain optional.
items.acceptance: An application supplies port/wire/selection recipes and changes themes without adding domain-specific branches to core rendering.

items.title: Accessibility style diagnostics
items.baseline_detail: Contrast checks, accessibility settings and widget/runtime harnesses exist; a comprehensive style validation view is not unified.
items.recommendation: Build on current checks and report evaluation assumptions; do not label a theme automatically WCAG compliant.
items.acceptance: Diagnostics identify actual failing color pairs and small targets, and distinguish AA focus-visible requirements from AAA focus-appearance criteria.

items.title: Locale-aware component presentation
items.baseline_detail: RTL helpers, Unicode text and widgets exist; integrated locale-aware style/content policy remains distributed.
items.recommendation: Keep translation/number formatting host-authored while style recipes accommodate expansion and intentional icon mirroring.
items.acceptance: Switching locale expands labels without clipping, mirrors only designated icons and preserves semantic keyboard reading order.

items.title: Declared renderer capabilities and fallback policy
items.baseline_detail: features.Usage and comptime feature analysis exist; software strips selected kinds, while ES2 omits params effects and ignores material handles.
requirements: fallback policy passed by the caller
items.recommendation: Extend existing usage reporting into a capability contract; do not make simple draw functions depend on a registry.
items.acceptance: A requested unsupported effect produces the caller-selected fallback or a diagnostic on every advertised backend, including ES2 and software.

items.title: Shared conservative paint bounds
items.baseline_detail: Visibility, damage culling and overlap tests use layout-space rect/clip bounds; transforms and three-sigma shadow growth are not incorporated consistently.
items.recommendation: Centralize pure bounds calculations and let callers supply conservative bounds for custom commands; disable unsafe optimizations when bounds are unknown.
items.acceptance: A node translated from offscreen to onscreen and a shadow whose sigma changes are neither culled nor incompletely repainted.

items.title: Alpha and color-transfer contracts
items.baseline_detail: RGBA8 colors and source-over rendering exist, but a general end-to-end contract covering imported images, effects and intermediate surfaces is not exposed.
items.recommendation: Make representation and transfer choices explicit at resource boundaries without requiring a managed resource subsystem for ordinary colors.
items.acceptance: Transparent colored texels and alpha gradients avoid dark fringes across import, filtering and compositing, with documented software/GPU tolerance.

items.title: Coherent paint, clip, text and hit coordinate spaces
items.baseline_detail: Style.transform affects quads; text/custom payloads, clipping and hit testing do not share that transform contract.
items.recommendation: Keep a clearly named paint-only mode if useful, and add a coherent subtree mode through explicit data and passes.
items.acceptance: A transformed labeled control paints, clips and responds at the same location; singular transforms have deterministic documented behavior.

items.title: Shared clip geometry across draw kinds
options: clip stack or equivalent indexed records
items.baseline_detail: Quads carry one rounded clip tuple, while text and custom commands carry only rectangular clips; nested rounded intersections are reduced incompletely.
items.recommendation: Expose plain clip records and bounded caller storage; optional builders may simplify nesting without hiding ownership.
items.acceptance: Nested rounded clips produce the same visible intersection for backgrounds, labels, images and participating custom content.

items.title: Composition of multiple visual decorations
items.baseline_detail: Stock params.x selects one feature per quad, so gradients, nine-slice mapping and patterned borders cannot all be selected on one node.
items.recommendation: Compose existing low-level primitives into ordered commands; make any recipe or cache optional and avoid combinatorial feature enums.
items.acceptance: One control displays a gradient, dashed border, image layer, rounded clipping and shadow together with stable ordering and bounded command count.

items.title: Existing compact RGBA colors
items.baseline_detail: types.Color provides packed RGBA8 and existing constructors used by normal Style and TextStyle fields.
items.recommendation: Retain the cheap value type and constructors as the everyday path.
items.acceptance: Existing source code and exact packed channel values retain their meaning after richer color options are introduced.

items.title: Additional color authoring and conversion
items.baseline_detail: The audited general color API is RGBA8; no broad typed authoring/conversion family was found.
items.recommendation: Offer pure constructors/converters that can run once or at comptime; do not put string parsing or color conversion in per-pixel loops.
items.acceptance: Reference conversion vectors round-trip within stated tolerances, and out-of-gamut input follows the documented policy.

items.title: Explicit color mixing and interpolation
items.baseline_detail: Two-color gradients and runtime color transitions exist, but selectable perceptual/linear and alpha-aware interpolation are not a unified contract.
items.recommendation: Use one explicit interpolation description for optional rich gradients and color motion while preserving the legacy result by default.
items.acceptance: Known midpoint colors and transparent-endpoint cases match the selected space in both static gradients and animated colors.

items.title: Managed wide-gamut output
items.baseline_detail: No general wide-gamut paint, surface and output contract was found in the audited RGBA8 pipeline.
items.recommendation: Add an optional complete output profile; retain SDR as a documented supported path.
items.acceptance: Wide-gamut content remains correctly tagged through rendering and capture, with an explicit consistent SDR conversion on unsupported targets.

items.title: HDR surfaces and tone mapping
items.baseline_detail: No HDR surface, headroom or tone-mapping API was found; current colors are packed RGBA8.
items.recommendation: Treat HDR as a complete optional backend/platform profile, informed by the draft specification rather than a mandatory core color expansion.
items.acceptance: SDR controls retain their intended luminance in an HDR scene and unsupported displays receive a documented tone-mapped result.

items.title: Solid fill and transparent background
items.baseline_detail: Style.fill is integrated, but transparent fill becomes a white tint for a nonwhite texture, conflating absence and literal transparency.
items.recommendation: Preserve direct solid fills and provide an unambiguous way to distinguish no fill, transparent fill and texture tint.
items.acceptance: An intentionally transparent image tint is distinguishable from an omitted tint without changing plain solid-fill output.

items.title: Ordered background paint layers
items.baseline_detail: Applications can stack separate nodes/custom draws, but the normal style has no general ordered background-list contract.
items.recommendation: Accept plain slices of layer descriptions and optionally provide recipes; keep the one-layer fast path.
items.acceptance: Transparent upper layers reveal lower layers in the declared order, and resizing updates geometry without changing ordering.

items.title: Background origin, clipping and attachment
items.baseline_detail: Fill/texture painting uses the existing node rectangle and inherited clipping; independent per-background reference boxes and attachments are not integrated.
items.recommendation: Define geometry per layer using explicit references; reserve viewport-fixed behavior for a declared profile.
items.acceptance: Changing padding or scrolling moves each layer according to its chosen reference box and attachment without moving unrelated content.

items.title: Linear gradient geometry
items.baseline_detail: features.linear provides a two-color gradient with an angle using node fill as the first color.
items.recommendation: Retain the two-color helper and lower richer linear brushes to the same simple path when possible.
items.acceptance: Existing angles preserve their results, while endpoint-based gradients remain stable under resizing and fractional transforms.

items.title: Radial gradient geometry
items.baseline_detail: features.radial supports two colors, normalized center and one circular radius.
items.recommendation: Keep the current circular representation as a fast case and add explicit elliptical geometry.
items.acceptance: Off-center elliptical gradients and zero-radius edge cases follow the documented result across backends.

items.title: Conic or sweep gradients
items.baseline_detail: The stock feature enum exposes linear and radial gradients but no conic feature.
items.recommendation: Add conic geometry through the shared brush interface instead of a widget-specific effect.
items.acceptance: The zero/full-turn seam, hard angular stops and rotated center produce consistent output without cracks.

items.title: Arbitrary stops and transition hints
items.baseline_detail: Existing gradient params hold only a start/end color and cannot encode a stop list.
items.recommendation: Take raw stop spans with explicit lifetime; optional cached lookup tables should remain an optimization layer.
items.acceptance: Hard stops stay sharp, invalid ordering is handled predictably, and many-stop gradients respect a declared capacity.

items.title: Gradient repetition and spread modes
items.baseline_detail: No shared gradient spread/tile mode was found in the current two-color feature helpers.
items.recommendation: Keep spread behavior independent of gradient geometry and document degenerate periods.
items.acceptance: Repeated gradients align at period boundaries under negative coordinates, fractional scaling and zero-length periods.

items.title: Foreground and overlay decoration
items.baseline_detail: Custom rendering supports underlay/overlay and inline commands; applications can author extra nodes in paint order.
items.recommendation: Offer optional helpers that emit ordinary ordered commands while preserving direct interleaving and the host render loop.
items.acceptance: A foreground decoration consistently covers content without intercepting input or requiring a second hidden event target.

items.title: Independent border edges
items.baseline_detail: Style has a single border width and color, plus existing circular radius data.
items.recommendation: Keep uniform borders compact; represent asymmetric edges as optional plain data that can lower to several primitives.
items.acceptance: Unequal widths and colors join without gaps at rounded corners and respect a documented logical-edge mapping.

items.title: Border patterns and continuous dash phase
items.baseline_detail: features.dashed and dotted exist; phase restarts by side and their selector excludes gradient/nine-slice features on the same quad.
items.recommendation: Preserve the existing simple patterns and add continuous perimeter semantics before adding ornamental styles.
items.acceptance: Dashes traverse rounded corners with a stable phase while the same control retains a gradient fill.

items.title: Inside, centered and outside borders
items.baseline_detail: No explicit public border alignment contract was found in the uniform border fields.
items.recommendation: Keep border placement distinct from stroke width and make content-padding consequences explicit.
items.acceptance: Changing alignment moves the stroke as specified, updates paint bounds, and changes layout only according to the documented policy.

items.title: Independent circular and elliptical corner radii
items.baseline_detail: Uniform radius and four independent scalar corner radii exist; elliptical radii and CSS-compatible normalization are not a complete contract.
items.recommendation: Retain circular fast paths and add one reusable radius-resolution function for richer geometry.
items.acceptance: Oversized asymmetric radii normalize without self-overlap and produce matching border, background, clip and shadow geometry.

items.title: Specialist corner shapes
items.baseline_detail: The current radius machinery represents circular rounded corners rather than a general corner-shape family.
items.recommendation: Use the extensible shape path first; the CSS corner-shape catalog is draft guidance rather than a compatibility commitment.
items.acceptance: A shaped corner gives matching fill, border and clip contours, including thick borders and concave variants.

items.title: Independent outline and focus-ring paint
items.baseline_detail: Focus.ring exposes a rectangle and applications/widgets can create extra nodes; theme focus commonly changes border fields.
items.recommendation: Expose a plain outline decoration that leaves layout unchanged; focus policy remains separate from drawing the ring.
items.acceptance: Showing a keyboard-focus ring causes no reflow and does not clip the ring or confuse focus with pointer hover.

items.title: Image fit and placement within a stable box
items.baseline_detail: widgets_image supports stretch/contain/cover; cover is centered and contain changes the actual node size.
items.recommendation: Provide independent destination geometry while retaining the current fitting helper for compatible callers.
items.acceptance: A fixed-size image box retains its layout dimensions across all fit modes and supports off-center cover cropping.

items.title: Source cropping and texture coordinates
items.baseline_detail: Style.uv and atlas-backed image rendering already provide texture subregion cropping.
items.recommendation: Retain direct UV access and add pure convenience conversions for pixel crops and orientation.
items.acceptance: A crop selects the intended texels without adjacent-atlas bleeding and retains its meaning under DPI scaling.

items.title: Independent image tint and alpha
items.baseline_detail: Textures multiply by node fill, with transparent fill used as a white-tint sentinel; inherited primitive opacity is also applied.
items.recommendation: Separate the image appearance inputs while keeping the old fill-multiplication path available for existing code.
items.acceptance: Image tint, background fill and image opacity can be changed independently without sentinel collisions.

items.title: Image tiling and texture address modes
items.baseline_detail: No portable style-level repeat contract was found; software sampling clamps coordinates and host GPU sampler configuration is lower level.
items.recommendation: Provide explicit pattern behavior with a software equivalent; do not assume a host sampler supplies consistent semantics.
items.acceptance: The same repeated image fills fractional-size regions consistently on software and accelerated backends, including negative offsets.

items.title: Nine-slice image skins
items.baseline_detail: features.nineSlice exists with stretched edges/center and destination cuts packed into 8-bit whole pixels.
items.recommendation: Preserve the compact stretched representation; richer cuts and tiling should use optional data rather than widening every quad.
items.acceptance: Corners retain intended dimensions under extreme aspect ratios, and large/subpixel cuts are not silently truncated.

items.title: Explicit texture sampling quality
items.baseline_detail: Stock shaders use nearest-texel conventions and software uses nearest/clamped sampling; mipmap generation alone does not establish sampled output.
requirements: sampler descriptor or explicit draw option
items.recommendation: Expose sampler behavior explicitly and preserve nearest for pixel-oriented callers.
items.acceptance: Upscaling and minification use the selected filter on each backend without atlas seams or implicit fallback changes.

items.title: Image resolution and device-scale selection
items.baseline_detail: Image atlas and mipmap generation modules exist; no shared declarative image-density/variant contract was established by the audit.
items.recommendation: Keep loading owned by the application and offer optional resolution helpers that do not start hidden IO.
items.acceptance: Switching display scale selects an appropriate resource while preserving logical size and the caller-controlled loading lifecycle.

items.title: Composable outer box shadows
items.baseline_detail: features.shadow is an analytic rounded-box Gaussian primitive, grown by three sigma; offset/spread are currently authored through a separate node.
items.recommendation: Provide an optional shadow helper/list that emits existing optimized primitives with explicit ordering.
items.acceptance: Changing spread, offset or blur repaints the full old/new extent and multiple shadows retain their declared order.

items.title: Inset box shadows
items.baseline_detail: The existing analytic shadow helper documents an outer blurred box; no built-in inset shadow contract was found.
items.recommendation: Implement inset shadows as an optional decoration using the shared shape machinery, with clear spread direction.
items.acceptance: Inset shadow coverage stays inside the chosen shape and handles negative spread and thick borders without seams.

items.title: Drop shadows from rendered content alpha
items.baseline_detail: Box shadows exist, but no generic retained content-alpha filter/layer command was found.
requirements: content source capture or equivalent fast path
items.recommendation: Keep content shadows distinct from box shadows and request offscreen resources explicitly when needed.
items.acceptance: A transparent icon casts its silhouette rather than its rectangular bounds, and source changes invalidate the shadow.

items.title: Reusable path geometry
items.baseline_detail: paths.Path provides move/line/quad/cubic/close, flattening and atlas emission; TinyVG decoding can supply arcs.
items.recommendation: Expose ergonomic plain-data paths and arc helpers without requiring callers to adopt a scene or resource manager.
items.acceptance: The same geometry can be filled, stroked and reused at multiple scales with a documented accuracy/capacity policy.

items.title: Path fill rules and brushes
items.baseline_detail: Path fill rules and coverage-atlas emission exist; rich brush integration is not a general normal-style path.
items.recommendation: Reuse path coverage with independent brushes so a color change need not rebuild geometry.
items.acceptance: Compound paths obey both fill rules, and changing paint preserves geometry while updating the correct pixels.

items.title: Stroke width, joins and caps
items.baseline_detail: paths strokes already support width, join and cap families; the normal styling interface does not expose a unified stroke brush.
items.recommendation: Retain the existing stroke engine and expose composable stroke values.
items.acceptance: Acute joins, zero-length segments and open caps produce bounded, correctly clipped output with the selected brush.

items.title: Dashed paths and dash phase
items.baseline_detail: Dashed/dotted rectangular border features exist, but general path dash arrays/offsets were not found in the path API.
items.recommendation: Extend the existing path engine; keep path dashing distinct from the current side-based border pattern.
items.acceptance: A dashed curved path maintains its phase through segment joins and closed seams, including zero entries under the documented policy.

items.title: Path markers and arrowheads
items.baseline_detail: Applications can draw custom path geometry, but no built-in marker/arrowhead attachment contract was found.
items.recommendation: Offer pure marker placement helpers useful for technical diagrams, with caller-provided geometry.
items.acceptance: Markers orient consistently at reversed/degenerate segments and scale according to their chosen units.

items.title: Non-scaling strokes and pixel-sized markers
items.baseline_detail: No general non-scaling stroke contract was found in existing path rasterization and paint transforms.
items.recommendation: Add an explicit stroke-space choice for zoomable engineering canvases.
items.acceptance: Zooming a drawing changes geometry size while the selected fixed-width strokes and markers retain the specified screen width.

items.title: Vector asset import and fidelity
items.baseline_detail: TinyVG is implemented but flattens gradients to their first color, ignores within-path variable width and skips text hints; full SVG import is absent.
items.recommendation: Extend the existing decoder and document an SVG subset separately; importers should feed plain drawing data.
items.acceptance: Unsupported asset features are reported rather than silently represented as full fidelity, and supported features match reference fixtures.

items.title: Existing custom shader materials
items.baseline_detail: Custom material handles and WGSL registration exist; ordinary Style carries them, but arbitrary GPU code has no automatic software equivalent and ES2 ignores materials.
items.recommendation: Preserve this real escape hatch and caller-controlled registration; improve diagnostics and portable fallback declarations.
items.acceptance: A custom material retains its render-loop ownership and receives a clear supported/fallback result on every selected backend.

items.title: Existing inline custom drawing and host interleaving
items.baseline_detail: Custom commands and drawUntilCustom let the application interleave drawing; current payloads expose rect/clip without shared opacity or transform.
items.recommendation: Keep the imperative command loop and raw drawing access; pass missing geometry information as data rather than introducing callbacks.
items.acceptance: Custom drawing interleaves in the same order as before and can honor transforms, clips and opacity using explicit data without hidden pass ownership.

items.title: Rectangular clip fast path
items.baseline_detail: Axis-aligned inherited rectangular clipping is present in layout and draw payloads.
items.recommendation: Preserve the direct rectangular fast path within the broader clip model.
items.acceptance: Nested, empty and fractional rectangular clips remain correct across background, text and custom draw commands.

items.title: Exact nested rounded clipping
items.baseline_detail: Quad carries one rounded clip tuple; nested clips collapse to one rect/radii pair and text/custom output lacks rounded geometry.
items.recommendation: Fix composition and propagation while retaining a single-rounded-clip specialization.
items.acceptance: Two offset rounded ancestors clip all descendant draw kinds to their true intersection without corner leaks.

items.title: Clipping to arbitrary geometry
items.baseline_detail: Path drawing exists, but the general clip pipeline is rectangular plus limited rounded data rather than a path clip contract.
requirements: backend stencil/mask lowering or software equivalent
items.recommendation: Reuse existing path geometry; expose clipping independently from painting and from optional hit shapes.
items.acceptance: A clipped-out region does not paint and follows the documented pointer policy, including nested path/rect clips.

items.title: Alpha and luminance masks
items.baseline_detail: No generic mask/layer command is present in the audited quads/text/custom command kinds.
items.recommendation: Add masks as an optional compositing operation with caller-controlled inputs and temporary storage.
items.acceptance: Alpha and luminance modes produce intentionally different results for colored masks and apply once to the intended group.

items.title: Mask placement and combination
items.baseline_detail: No built-in mask stack or mask-border contract was found.
items.recommendation: Use plain mask-layer spans and explicit operators; keep unused mask features outside small-target builds.
items.acceptance: Layer combinations obey order and coordinate spaces and fail predictably when the supplied capacity is exceeded.

items.title: Complete 2D affine transform styling
items.baseline_detail: Style.transform provides inherited center-based affine quad transforms, but text, clips, hit testing and pure comptime painting are limited.
items.recommendation: Retain plain affine matrices and add origin/reference-box helpers plus coherent subtree behavior.
items.acceptance: Rotated/scaled/skewed controls keep label, decoration, clip and input geometry aligned without silently changing surrounding layout.

items.title: Optional perspective and 3D composition
items.baseline_detail: The built-in transform is affine 2D; custom host rendering can supply independent 3D content but is not a built-in subtree transform.
requirements: projective clipping and inverse input mapping
items.recommendation: Add a separate optional capability only after 2D semantics are sound; preserve host-rendered 3D as an existing route.
items.acceptance: Perspective descendants have defined occlusion, clipping, backface and input behavior without corrupting surrounding 2D ordering.

items.title: Existing inherited per-primitive opacity
items.baseline_detail: Style.opacity multiplies ancestor values onto each quad and text run; custom commands do not carry that opacity.
items.recommendation: Keep the existing cheap behavior named and documented; do not silently redefine it as group opacity.
items.acceptance: Existing alpha composition stays stable, while custom content receives enough information to honor the same intended primitive alpha.

items.title: Exact opacity of a completed subtree
items.baseline_detail: Inherited primitive alpha exists, but DrawList has no retained offscreen group/layer command.
items.recommendation: Add group opacity separately, with explicit resource costs and optimization only when pixel-equivalent.
items.acceptance: Two overlapping opaque children faded as one group match flatten-then-fade output, including nested opacity and text.

items.title: Explicit offscreen layer operations
items.baseline_detail: Applications already own passes and can render UI into a texture; there is no generic retained layer/filter command in the built-in list.
items.recommendation: Expose operations and requirements to the host; an optional pool may be provided without taking over pass ownership.
items.acceptance: A layer reports its required bounds/format/storage and can execute using caller-managed resources, with deterministic capacity failure.

items.title: Local stacking and isolated groups
items.baseline_detail: overlay.Layers uses 256 global numeric levels inheriting parent maximum; layered paint/hit helpers exist but do not implement isolated nested stacking contexts.
items.recommendation: Retain global layers and add local isolation only where requested; avoid a mandatory DOM-like stacking model.
items.acceptance: A nested isolated group cannot accidentally interleave its children with outside content, and the visible top target wins hit testing.

items.title: Artistic blend modes
items.baseline_detail: Stock source-over blending exists; no general built-in artistic blend-mode field/group contract was found.
items.recommendation: Separate artistic blending from alpha compositing and expose background-layer versus group scope.
items.acceptance: Reference source/backdrop colors match each mode, including transparent inputs and isolation boundaries.

items.title: Porter-Duff and related compositing operators
items.baseline_detail: Normal stock rendering provides over blending; other general compositing operators are not exposed as portable draw operations.
items.recommendation: Keep source-over as the ordinary fast path and add explicit advanced operators for canvas/effect use.
items.acceptance: Operator fixtures agree with defined premultiplied-alpha equations and do not modify pixels outside the intended bounds.

items.title: Foreground color filters
items.baseline_detail: Custom GPU materials can implement color operations, but no portable built-in filter-chain contract is present.
items.recommendation: Offer pure color-operation descriptions and fuse compatible operations without promising arbitrary chains fit one pass.
items.acceptance: Operation order is preserved, neutral filters leave output unchanged, and fused output matches the unfused reference.

items.title: General foreground blur
items.baseline_detail: An analytic blurred box-shadow primitive exists; it is not a general image/subtree blur operation.
items.recommendation: Add general blur separately from the optimized box shadow, with explicit area and resource cost.
items.acceptance: Blurred content has correct edge behavior and extent; changing sigma or source pixels invalidates all affected output.

items.title: Bounded backdrop filtering
items.baseline_detail: No retained backdrop-read/filter command or backdrop dependency tracking was found.
items.recommendation: Document chosen native semantics because backdrop-root standardization remains unsettled; never infer freshness from the panel style alone.
items.acceptance: Moving content behind an unchanged panel refreshes the correct blur, including nesting, clipping and explicit unsupported-backend fallback.

items.title: Optional filter graph extensions
items.baseline_detail: Custom materials and host rendering are existing escape hatches; no portable built-in graph of these filter operations was found.
items.recommendation: Use optional extensions or host-authored operations; do not add a core widget field for every specialist effect.
items.acceptance: Each operation declares inputs, bounds and backend requirements, and unsupported nodes fail or use a caller-selected fallback predictably.

items.title: Existing property tweening with semantic invalidation
items.baseline_detail: SIMD Tweens and Frame.transition exist; retargeting starts from the current value and reusing the same target preserves the current leg.
items.recommendation: Keep raw scalar tween functions usable; optional property adapters may classify invalidation without hiding frame control.
items.acceptance: Retargeting is continuous, and animating only a paint color does not force layout or text shaping.

items.title: Extended easing functions
items.baseline_detail: Tweens has six coefficient-table easing curves; general cubic-bezier/step/piecewise curves are not exposed.
items.recommendation: Preserve the existing SIMD coefficient path and add opt-in curve kinds or compiled tables for richer easing.
items.acceptance: Endpoint, step-boundary and out-of-range behavior is defined, and supplied curves do not change existing curve results.

items.title: Existing spring motion and control
items.baseline_detail: Anims stores spring position, velocity, target, stiffness and damping in columns; Frame integrates reduced-motion landing.
items.recommendation: Expose useful existing controls and document time-step/rest behavior without replacing the spring engine.
items.acceptance: Springs settle deterministically under the documented time-step policy, retarget without unintended jumps, and stop requesting frames when at rest.

items.title: Extended keyframe playback
items.baseline_detail: Scalar keyframe sampling and Frame.sequence already exist; general playback direction/repetition/fill controls are not a complete contract.
items.recommendation: Keep sampling a pure function of caller time and add optional playback helpers around it.
items.acceptance: Repeat boundaries, reverse/alternate direction, zero-duration segments and pause/resume produce deterministic sampled values.

items.title: Color transitions with explicit interpolation
items.baseline_detail: Runtime color transitions are implemented, but selectable perceptual and premultiplied interpolation are not a shared public contract.
items.recommendation: Extend the existing helper with an explicit interpolation choice and preserve legacy defaults.
items.acceptance: Animated transparent colors avoid fringes and selected midpoint colors match the corresponding static gradient interpolation.

items.title: Layout transition and FLIP expansion
items.baseline_detail: FLIP moves registered subtree positions before finalize so clips/hits follow displayed positions; size changes are explicitly not animated.
items.recommendation: Keep position FLIP and its explicit pass; add size behavior only after deciding whether content relayouts or is visually scaled.
items.acceptance: Nested interrupted transitions retain correct displayed positions, and any size animation has documented text/layout and hit-target behavior.

items.title: Motion along a path
items.baseline_detail: Path geometry and scalar animation exist, but no built-in path-following placement helper was found.
items.recommendation: Provide a pure path-position sampler that callers can compose with existing animation and drawing.
items.acceptance: Distance-based motion and tangent rotation remain stable across segment joins and documented zero-length path cases.

items.title: Compatible path and shape morphing
items.baseline_detail: Paths and scalar keyframes exist, but no general topology-aware path morph contract was found.
items.recommendation: Start with matching topology and an explicit fallback; avoid silently inventing correspondence between unrelated shapes.
items.acceptance: Compatible paths interpolate without topology changes, while incompatible paths follow the documented discrete/crossfade choice.

items.title: Existing reduced-motion and idle behavior
items.baseline_detail: Settings and runtime spring/tween/sequence/FLIP helpers already integrate reduced motion and frame wake behavior.
items.recommendation: Retain existing accessibility behavior in every new motion helper and preserve caller control of the event loop.
items.acceptance: Enabling reduced motion during active motion lands at a valid end state and leaves no unnecessary continuous frame scheduling.

items.title: Explicit playback lifecycle and completion
items.baseline_detail: Tweens retarget continuously and sweep unseen entries; current bounded slot behavior can reuse the last row when capacity is exceeded.
items.recommendation: Expose lifecycle state as data rather than requiring callbacks, and make capacity policy visible to callers.
items.acceptance: Cancellation, hiding and capacity exhaustion do not silently animate an unrelated control, and completion can be consumed without hidden event dispatch.

items.title: Pixel snapping and fractional geometry
items.baseline_detail: layout.finalize snaps layout rectangles; the complete relationship among nested transforms, fractional edges and device-scale output needs a shared contract.
items.recommendation: Keep logical geometry explicit and apply a documented snapping policy without repeated ancestor rounding.
items.acceptance: A one-device-pixel line remains stable at supported scales, and nested fractional transforms do not accumulate avoidable alignment drift.

items.title: Shape and clip antialiasing policy
items.baseline_detail: Rounded quad and path coverage rendering exist, but a portable author-visible quality policy across all shapes and clips is not unified.
items.recommendation: Expose quality only where it changes a meaningful choice; preserve good defaults and exact rectangular fast paths.
items.acceptance: Thin shapes and nested clip edges avoid double-darkening/seams, with a documented software/GPU comparison tolerance.

items.title: Optional window-system materials
items.baseline_detail: Custom host rendering exists, but no built-in native visual-effect/Mica material bridge was established by the audit.
items.recommendation: Offer optional host-side adapters; keep native window materials separate from in-app backdrop blur.
items.acceptance: Unsupported platforms and reduced-transparency/high-contrast conditions select a readable explicit fallback without changing core renderer ownership.

items.title: Effect quality and resource limits
items.baseline_detail: Caller-owned bounded buffers and feature stripping are established architecture, but new effects need explicit compatible limits and overflow behavior.
items.recommendation: Extend the existing bounded-memory philosophy; let callers choose budgets and quality rather than allocating hidden full-window surfaces.
items.acceptance: Every effect exposes or validates required capacity and exceeding it never leaves partially rendered or semantically ambiguous output.

items.title: Existing texture-in and render-to-texture routes
items.baseline_detail: The custom-rendering guide documents texture input/output with host-owned device, queue, pass and targets; textured quads can be transformed.
items.recommendation: Retain these raw interop operations and build optional effects from them without replacing the host render loop.
items.acceptance: A host-produced texture and a UI-produced texture compose with ordinary draws under explicit lifetime, alpha and pass-order contracts.
